summary: Woman in her 20s from New Mexico fell ~90 ft down a cliff face while taking photos on a day hike; concussion and badly broken leg; crawled to the Animas River bank and flagged passing trains over two days; spotted Monday by a passenger on Durango & Silverton engine No. 461; railroad crew waded the river with supplies and blankets; airlifted to Montrose Hospital.
location: Animas River bank ~5 miles south of Silverton (Deer Park area)
responding_agency: Silverton Medical Rescue Team; San Juan County Search and Rescue; CareFlight; Durango & Silverton Narrow Gauge Railroad crew
notes: Date inference: Trains.com wire (published ~10/12/2022) says spotted 'on Monday'; 2022-10-10 was a Monday; NPR story (10/23/2022) says rescue 'earlier this month' after two days trapped. Reported missing Sunday 10/9. Track inspector Delton Henry stopped the motor car and communicated with her across the river; engineer/fireman Nick and Kylah Breeden (Kylah a Durango FD paramedic) waded the Animas to reach her; D&SNG superintendent Darren Whitten requested SAR. She lost consciousness after the fall, had no emergency supplies and no clothing for nights outdoors during a cold snap. Merged 2026-09-11 (run 70): iHeart/SJC-OEM mirror of the train-crew rescue confirms father Anthony Montoya naming her; she was airlifted with a broken leg and hip injury and flown to a New Mexico hospital for surgery.
